question: Should OpenClaw intentionally allow explicit `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` on non-loopback/private-ingress binds, and under what guardrails?
rationale: The request weakens a reachable Gateway auth boundary and conflicts with current startup guard behavior, so automation cannot choose the security posture safely.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Default
options.body: Continue requiring token/password or trusted-proxy auth for non-loopback binds and align private-ingress docs to that boundary.

options.title: Add Explicit Private-Ingress No-Auth Mode
options.body: Allow `auth.mode="none"` on non-loopback binds only with maintainer-approved wording, audit warnings, and focused CLI/runtime tests.

recommendation.title: Keep Fail-Closed Default
recommendation.body: Continue requiring token/password or trusted-proxy auth for non-loopback binds and align private-ingress docs to that boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent hardening history makes this the best available owner for a security-boundary decision around exposed no-auth startup.
